bib.title: Align before Fuse: Vision and Language Representation Learning with Momentum Distillation

legacy_report:
SOURCE: Align before Fuse: Vision and Language Representation Learning with Momentum Distillation. Junnan Li, Ramprasaath R. Selvaraju, Akhilesh D. Gotmare, Shafiq Joty, Caiming Xiong, Steven C.H. Hoi (Salesforce Research). NeurIPS 2021 (arXiv:2107.07651v2).

COVERAGE: I read all 54,878 of 54,878 chars, which covers pp.1–16: the body, all 8 tables, and appendices A–E. I only skimmed the reference list.

CLAIMS
- claim: Detectors are the cost the paper removes. They need box annotations to train and high-resolution input at inference, and ALBEF instead uses a detector-free ViT-B/16 on 256² crops in pretraining and 384² in fine-tuning.
  number: 600×1000
  setup: This is the motivation for dropping detectors. The paper never runs a detector-based ALBEF, so the size of the cost is not measured.
  quote: "The object detector is both annotation-expensive and compute-expensive, because it requires bounding box annotations during pre-training, and high-resolution (e.g. 600×1000) images during inference"
  where: p.1
- claim: Adding ITC (a contrastive loss on the separate image and text encoders, applied before cross-attention fusion) to MLM+ITM gives the largest single gain in the ablation. Contrastive hard negatives and MoD each add smaller gains.
  number: Flickr TR 93.96→96.55; NLVR2 77.51→79.88; VQA 71.40→73.29. The full model reaches VQA 74.54.
  setup: Table 1, 4M images. TR and IR are the mean of R@1, R@5 and R@10. NLVR2 is test-P, VQA is test-dev.
  quote: "MLM + ITM 93.96 88.55 77.06 77.51 71.40 / ITC + MLM + ITM 96.55 91.69 79.15 79.88 73.29"
  where: p.7, Table 1
- claim: Momentum distillation trains the model against soft targets from an EMA copy of itself, so web captions that are wrong or incomplete are not punished as hard errors. It adds only small gains.
  number: α=0.4 and momentum 0.995. VQA rises 73.81→74.06 with ITC-MoD and to 74.42 with MLM-MoD as well.
  setup: Table 1, 4M images. The queue holds 65,536 entries. α values of 0.3, 0.4 and 0.5 perform about the same.
  quote: "With MoD, the model is not penalized for producing other reasonable outputs that are different from the web annotation."
  where: p.2 (quote); p.5 (hyperparameters); p.7 (numbers)
- claim: Pretraining data is 4M images (5.1M pairs from CC, SBU, COCO and VG, following UNITER) or 14.1M once the noisier CC12M is added. Going to 14M lifts every task.
  number: 4.0M / 14.1M
  setup: Some dataset URLs no longer resolved. Training ran 30 epochs at batch 512 on 8 A100s.
  quote: "The total number of unique images is 4.0M, and the number of image-text pairs is 5.1M ... increasing the total number of images to 14.1M"
  where: p.5
- claim: Headline comparison with VILLA. The abstract's +2.37 (VQA) and +3.84 (NLVR2) come from the 14M model. With the same 4M data the margins are smaller.
  number: VQA test-std 76.04 (14M) and 74.70 (4M) vs VILLA 73.67. NLVR2 test-P 83.14 and 80.50 vs 79.30. UNITER scores 72.91 and 77.85.
  setup: Table 4. VQA is posed as answer generation with a 6-layer decoder limited to 3,192 candidate answers.
  quote: "Compared to VILLA [8], ALBEF achieves absolute improvements of 2.37% on VQA test-std, 3.84% on NLVR2 test-P, and 1.88% on SNLI-VE test."
  where: p.8
- claim: In retrieval, the 4M model beats UNITER, and the 14M model matches or beats ALIGN, which was trained on 1.2B images. Inference first ranks all pairs by cheap ITC similarity, then rescores only the top-k with ITM. Results barely change with k, and the paper says it is >10× faster than VILLA on NLVR2.
  number: Flickr fine-tuned TR R@1 94.3 (4M) and 95.9 (14M) vs UNITER 87.3 and ALIGN 95.3. Zero-shot TR R@1 94.1 (14M) vs CLIP 88.0 (400M). Mean TR for k=16/128/256 is 98.60/98.57/98.57.
  setup: Tables 2, 3 and 6. Zero-shot Flickr uses the model fine-tuned on COCO.
  quote: "it also enjoys much faster inference speed compared to most existing methods (>10 times faster than VILLA on NLVR2)"
  where: p.8; Table 6 on p.9

LIMITS
- No speed numbers are given. There is no timing table, hardware, or batch setting behind the ">10×" claim.
- No detector-based ALBEF exists to separate the effect of dropping the detector from the effect of ITC.
- "Zero-shot" Flickr retrieval means fine-tuned on COCO, not truly zero-shot.
- The headline gains depend on 14M images vs VILLA's 4M.
- The authors concede that SNLI-VE "should be interpreted with caution because its test data has been reported to be noisy". RefCOCO+ val/test images were seen during pretraining, and decontamination is "left as future work" (p.13).
- The mutual-information section is an interpretation, not a proof of gains.
- The social-impacts section notes private or harmful content in web data.
- Dated details: the encoder is ViT-B/16 + BERT-base at about 210M parameters, there is no generative LM, and the comparisons stop at 2021 (ViLT, VinVL era).

BUILDS ON: UNITER (Chen et al., ECCV 2020), VILLA (Gan et al., NeurIPS 2020), OSCAR (Li et al., ECCV 2020), LXMERT (Tan & Bansal, EMNLP 2019), CLIP (Radford et al., arXiv 2021), ALIGN (Jia et al., arXiv 2021), ViLT (Kim et al., arXiv 2021; detector-free but weaker), MoCo queues (He et al., CVPR 2020), ViT (Dosovitskiy et al., ICLR 2021) with DeiT weights (Touvron et al., 2020), BERT (Devlin et al., NAACL 2019), Mean Teacher (Tarvainen & Valpola, NIPS 2017), distillation (Hinton et al., 2015), CC12M (Changpinyo et al., CVPR 2021).

CODE: none in the PDF (repo: https://github.com/salesforce/ALBEF).

FIGURES: Fig. 1, p.3: "Illustration of ALBEF. It consists of an image encoder, a text encoder, and a multimodal encoder..." In one diagram it shows ITC acting on the encoders' [CLS] outputs before 6 cross-attention layers, ITM/MLM after fusion, hard negatives, and the momentum model. That is the "align, then fuse" lineage point in a single picture.

PROBLEMS: Extraction was clean. Table text was flattened but readable. No embedded instructions.
